catalog_quote: [Les homographes] ... -tala₁ [-tala]: 1) lire, 2) compter / -tala₂ [-tála]: 1) regarder, observer, 2) vérifier. Dans le cas de bie, les deux mots se prononcent de manière identique. Mais le mot -tala a deux prononciations (schémas tonal) différentes. (Voir: 4. transcription phonétique ci-dessous) ... [4. La transcription phonétique] La transcription phonétique entre crochets suit chaque entrée lexicale et sa variante éventuelle. Tout accent aigu (á) sur une voyelle indique un ton haut, et l'absence d'un accent indique soit un ton bas, soit un ton qui peut changer selon le contexte de la phrase. (La voyelle finale des mots est souvent avalé dans le parler, rendant difficile la tâche d’identifier clairement le ton sur cette voyelle). Ex.: mukpere [mukpɛ́rɛ́] machette nka [ŋká] antilope me [mɛ] moi -nama [-nama] suivre, obéir

new_statements.quote: La transcription phonétique entre crochets suit chaque entrée lexicale et sa variante éventuelle. Tout accent aigu (á) sur une voyelle indique un ton haut, et l'absence d'un accent indique soit un ton bas, soit un ton qui peut changer selon le contexte de la phrase. (La voyelle finale des mots est souvent avalé dans le parler, rendant difficile la tâche d'identifier clairement le ton sur cette voyelle). Ex. : mukpere [mukpɛ́rɛ́] machette; nka [ŋká] antilope; me [mɛ] moi; -nama [-nama] suivre, obéir
new_statements.translation: The phonetic transcription in square brackets follows each lexical entry and its possible variant. Any acute accent (á) over a vowel indicates a high tone, and the absence of an accent indicates either a low tone or a tone that can change depending on the context of the sentence. (The final vowel of words is often swallowed in speech, making it difficult to clearly identify the tone on that vowel). E.g. mukpere [mukpɛ́rɛ́] machete; nka [ŋká] antelope; me [mɛ] me; -nama [-nama] follow, obey. (The site's own English version.)

new_statements.rule_in_words: Teke-Tyee is presented as a tone language: high tone is marked by an acute accent in the dictionary's phonetic transcriptions, unmarked vowels are low-toned or carry a tone that varies with sentence context, and tone distinguishes otherwise identical words (-tala 'read/count' vs -tála 'look'). The source says nothing about stress or accentual prominence; no stress placement rule is given.
new_statements.exceptions: Word-final vowels are often elided in speech, so their tone is hard to identify; unmarked tones may change with sentence context.
new_statements.domain_note: Dictionary citation forms (nouns and verb stems cited without the infinitive prefix o-); lexical word tone, with acknowledged sentence-level tone changes. The dictionary covers the Tyɛɛ of the Pool (Kimba, Vindza) and Bouenza (Kingoué) departments.
new_statements.identity_note: Teke-Tyee [tyx] = Glottolog teke1276 (alt. names Tee, Tyɛɛ, Kwe, West Teke). The quoted source is the SIL-Congo Teke-Tyee dictionary (2022) whose foreword says it covers the Tyɛɛ of the Pool (Kimba, Vindza districts) and Bouenza (Kingoué district) and notes that Teke-Laali [lli] is close; Wikipedia lumps Tyee with Tsaayi [tyi], Laali [lli] and Yaa [iyx] as 'West Teke' (B73), which Glottolog splits into separate languages. The still-to-obtain Mouandza 2002 describes Yaa, not Tyee.

tone_statements.citation: Laman, Karl Edward. 1927. The musical tone of the Teke language. In Festschrift Meinhof: sprachwissenschaftliche und andere Studien, 118-124. Hamburg: Kommissionsverlag von L. Friederichsen & Co. (Glottolog: Glückstadt & Hamburg: J.J. Augustin). Open scan:https://archive.org/details/festschriftmeinh00unse(OCLC 13218063 / 1713348).
tone_statements.quote: The following are the essential tones of Teke. A high-level tone: ... A semi-high-level tone: ... A semi-low-level tone: ... A low-level tone: ... A very high-level and a very low-level tone occurs sometimes. A high-semi-high falling tone: ... A high-semi-low falling tone: ... A semi-low-semi-high rising tone: ... A rising-falling tone: ... A falling-rising tone: ... In connected speech there are also other rising and falling tones ... With regard to the tone-series there are in Teke two very distinct tone-series: a hightone-series and a lowtone-series.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 120-121, 'essential tones of Teke' list and opening of the tone-series section
tone_statements.summary: 1927 phonetic account: four level grades (high, semi-high, semi-low, low) plus falling, rising and compound syllable tones; stems in two tone-series (high, low); no closed count; minimal pairs.

sources.note: Nothing on stress. The dedicated Phonology and Grammar pages are empty placeholders ('Contenu à venir dans le proche avenir'). The 'Entries explained' page states that acute accent marks high tone in the phonetic transcription and unmarked vowels are low or context-variable tone; tone distinguishes homographs (-tala 'lire/compter' vs -tála 'regarder'). Alphabet page: 5 vowels, length by doubling, final nasalisation by tilde; no accent/stress diacritic.
